shouldFix.title: An input corpus whose three initial states contain no initial state
shouldFix.finding: The artifact's purpose is to 'Continue leftover-design of OBL-G16-FX-AUTHORING by naming initial states of the three live G16 v2 corpus classes', and whatIsAuthored claims 'Three named initial states'. Each of the three records holds exactly four fields: an id that is a slug of the class name, memberVerbatim which is the class name, fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED, and assertsNamedNotAuthored which is a one-element list containing the class name again. There is no condition, variant, position, scenario or input of any kind. The three records are distinguished from one another by nothing except which class they restate, so nothing in the artifact says what state a G16 harness would start in.
shouldFix.againstTheDocumentClass: I checked whether this is the input-corpus shape and it is not. Four siblings carry substantive per-state content: permission-fx5-input-corpus.v2 gives four states each with a positionNamed such as 'revocation before acceptance'; permission-fx11-input-corpus.v2 gives a state with crashBetween ICI and ICO, doesNotRetry, treatsGenerationAsRevoked; doctor-fc-ro-input-corpus.v3 gives fourteen states each with variantClass, degradedCase, consentClass and auditWrite; permission-r6-r10-input-corpus.v2 gives two states each with race, outcome and whyDeterministic. In every one the NOT-AUTHORED markers hang off a state that has been named. Here the markers hang off nothing.
shouldFix.addsNothingOverTheCatalogItConsumes: g16-named-corpus-catalog.v1, already accepted and pinned by this artifact, carries per class an id, memberVerbatim, exactByteIntentVerbatim, passPropertyVerbatim, fixtureBytes and inventedIdentifiers. This artifact's per-state fields are a strict subset of that. So on the state axis it advances OBL-G16-FX-AUTHORING's leftover-design by nothing a later authoring cycle could not already read from the catalog.
shouldFix.theMaterialWasAvailable: The obvious defence is that naming a G16 initial state would require inventing a CI provider, YAML or path filter, which the dispatch forbids. It does not. G16 v2's own exactByteIntent supplies namable axes for each class that are not CI encodings: for change-impact-matrix, change-set units of add, delete, rename and byte-change across the four D-002 platforms with TypeScript as the only language role, plus the unrelated-change case; for forced-mutations, five named mutation kinds — omitted dependency, omitted owner, missing component declaration, owner outside the comparison-basis universe, and incomplete or invalid universe construction; for aggregate-release, two named selections, component-new/core-unchanged and core-new/component-unchanged. Those are precisely the shape of fx5's four revocation positions. The artifact pins the source that contains them and carried none.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing stated is false, no row moves, required-now is untouched, the artifact binds NOTHING and is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, and every prohibition is honoured. The defect is that the deliverable is empty against its own stated purpose, not that anything in it is wrong.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Give each of the three records at least one named initial state drawn from G16 v2's exactByteIntent — the five mutation kinds and the two release selections are already enumerated there — with the NOT-AUTHORED markers attached to those named states rather than to the class name.
shouldFix.notAssertedByThisFinding: I do not author any initial state, propose fixture bytes, name a CI encoding, or assert how many states each class should carry. The finding is that records called initial states contain none.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Seventeen attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject 86d3c402 at 0444, 5570 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; the artifact's own head field equals it; live required-now 26 of 26; live DR-121 token OPEN; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All nine cited pins reproduce, and every 64-hex string in the artifact is one of those nine, so no authored fixture digest hides among them. Every prohibition is honoured and I tested the two that matter by content rather than keyword: no fixture bytes, and no reserved CI encodings — zero YAML, zero .yml or .yaml references, zero CI provider names, zero cache or path-filter mentions, zero command literals. Rust, G13, D9 and §7.1 appear only as refusals, and SATISFIED and QUALIFIED appear zero times. The dispatch's equality attack fails: the three classes are identical four ways, each state's own assertion names only its own class, and the slash-joined first class is held whole rather than decomposed. The finding is the artifact's own deliverable. It exists to name initial states — that is its purpose field and its whatIsAuthored claim — and its three records contain none. Each holds a slug of the class name, the class name, a NOT-AUTHORED marker, and the class name again; nothing distinguishes the three except which class they restate. I checked whether that is the document class's shape and it is not: permission-fx5 gives four states each with a named revocation position, permission-fx11 gives a state with crashBetween ICI and ICO and its behavioural flags, doctor-fc-ro gives fourteen states with variantClass, degradedCase, consentClass and auditWrite, and permission-r6-r10 gives two states with race, outcome and whyDeterministic. In every sibling the NOT-AUTHORED markers hang off a state that has been named; here they hang off nothing. The artifact is also a strict subset of the catalog it consumes, which carries exactByteIntentVerbatim and passPropertyVerbatim per class, so on the state axis it advances the leftover-design by nothing a later authoring cycle could not already read there. I tested the strongest defence — that naming a G16 initial state would require inventing a CI encoding — and it fails: G16 v2's own exactByteIntent already enumerates five mutation kinds for forced-mutations, two selections for aggregate-release, and change-set units across four platforms for change-impact-matrix, none of which is a CI encoding. The material was in a source the artifact pins. It is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker because nothing stated is false and no obligation is closed or misclassified. Two things I declined to raise are recorded so the bar can be checked: the artifact calls itself 'this catalog' three times while being an input corpus, which looked like template drift until I found the same usage in doctor-fc-ro-input-corpus.v3, an input corpus I accepted; and it carries no recordedInputs or remeasurementClause, which is the input-corpus form rather than an omission, as the dispatch's own 'head is not 5d5d778' phrasing reflects. One disclosure: all four Claude-lane verdicts this artifact pins are my lane's and two are mine from earlier in this session, and this finding came from a document-class comparison rather than from the dispatch's attack list — had I stopped at the listed attacks, this would have been an ACCEPT.
